rationale: C14 is a concrete and material drafting template for the child. Both directives prescribe, in the same sequence, a dignitary's coat of arms, seal, and color and flag; use closely matching heraldic language; specify dimensions according to military and naval custom; incorporate accompanying illustrations and specifications; reserve the designs exclusively to represent the office; and revoke or supersede an earlier directive. C20 likely supplied the updated star-count predicate and July 4, 1959 effective date, while C17 shares only the narrower machinery for approving a flag design incorporated into an order.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The Coat of Arms of the President of the United States shall be of the following design: SHIELD: Paleways of thirteen pieces argent and gules, a chief azure; upon the breast of an American eagle displayed holding in his dexter talon an olive branch... and in his beak a white scroll inscribed "E PLURIBUS UNUM" sable.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Coat of Arms of the Vice President of the United States shall be of the following design: SHIELD: Paleways of thirteen pieces argent and gules, a chief azure; upon the breast of an American eagle with wings displayed and inverted holding in his dexter talon an olive branch... in his beak a yellow scroll inscribed "E PLURIBUS UNUM" sable.
shared_material.explanation: Distinctive heraldic formulation is reused with adaptations to the presidential emblem.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The Seal of the President of the United States shall consist of the Coat of Arms encircled by the words "Seal of the President of the United States."
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Seal of the Vice President of the United States shall consist the Coat of Arms encircled by the words "Vice President of the United States."
shared_material.explanation: The seal provision is nearly identical, substituting the office and surrounding inscription.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The Color and Flag of the President of the United States shall consist of a dark blue rectangular background of sizes and proportions to conform to military and naval custom, on which shall appear the Coat of Arms of the President in proper colors. The proportions of the elements of the Coat of Arms shall be in direct relation to the hoist, and the fly shall vary according to the customs of the military and naval services.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Color and Flag of the Vice President of the United States shall consist of a white rectangular background of sizes and proportions to conform to military and naval custom, on which shall appear the Coat of Arms of the Vice President in proper colors. The proportion of the elements of the Coat of Arms shall be in direct relation to the hoist, and the fly shall vary according to the customs of the military and naval services.
shared_material.explanation: This is extensive near-verbatim reuse of a distinctive technical specification, changing chiefly the office and background color.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The Coat of Arms, Seal, and Color and Flag shall be as described herein and as set forth in the illustrations and specifications which accompany this order and which are hereby made a part thereof. These designs shall be used to represent the President of the United States exclusively.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Coat of Arms, Seal, and Color and Flag shall be as described herein and as set forth in the illustrations and specifications which accompany this order and which are hereby made a part thereof. These designs shall be used to represent the Vice President of the United States exclusively.
shared_material.explanation: The incorporation and exclusive-use provisions are reproduced almost word for word.
